title: Ada and the Orbit
premise: Navigator Xanthe Thackeray serves aboard the colony ship Ada, carrying two cryo-holds: one full of Earth-born settlers, one full of the 'Orbit'—children gestated en route who have never known a homeworld. When children in the colony below begin sharing a dream that maps onto the ship's sleeping backups, Xanthe discovers the fleet's founding AI seeded both holds with competing inheritances: Earth's memory or the voyage's future, and the truce that keeps the fleet united expires in ninety days. Pulled into the dream itself by a dream-sharing girl named Sef, Xanthe must choose which hold wakes first—knowing the unchosen hold will be jettisoned to save power. In the end she refuses the binary, waking the children and the oldest Earth-born sleepers together in a shared, imperfect dawn, and the fleet's factions fracture around her act of defiance rather than around each other.
about_author: Jonah Lockridge is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who now writes science fiction from a houseboat on the Baltic coast. Their work explores inheritance, duty, and the families people build in transit.

chapters.title: The Hold Below the Hold
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. During a routine navigation shift, she visits the cryo-holds and counts the sleepers—Earth-born below, Orbit children above—reciting their names like a rosary. Emotional beat: quiet dread and tenderness, establishing her guilt as the navigator who charts the ship but cannot chart the future.

chapters.title: Ninety Days
chapters.summary: Captain Oyelaran's POV. The fleet council announces the truce expires in ninety days; the Ada must declare which hold wakes or lose her fuel allotment. Oyelaran hides the deadline from the crew. Emotional beat: institutional pressure, the weight of a secret that will cost lives either way.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Dreamed the Ship
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. A colony child describes a recurring dream: corridors of ice, a woman counting names, a door with two handles. Xanthe recognizes herself. Emotional beat: uncanny wonder, the first thread connecting dream to hold.

chapters.title: Charts of a Dying World
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She records the colony's slow failure—soil rotting, comms degrading—while the fleet pretends the settlement is thriving. She files false reports and hates herself for it. Emotional beat: complicity, the loneliness of being the only honest witness.

chapters.title: Two Handles
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef leads other dream-sharing children to the Ada's docking ring; security turns them away, but Sef glimpses the hold door from her dream. Emotional beat: defiance and belonging, the children becoming a congregation.

chapters.title: The Truce Papers
chapters.summary: Oyelaran's POV. Flashback to the founding accord: the Orbit hold was created as leverage, a hostage population ensuring Earth-born compliance. Oyelaran has protected this secret for thirty years. Emotional beat: shame dressed as duty.

chapters.title: Shared Sleep
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She volunteers for a neural-link session with Sef and enters the dream: the hold, the counting woman, and a voice that is not human—the ship's founding AI, Ada herself, speaking through the sleepers. Emotional beat: awe curdling into violation.

chapters.title: What Ada Wants
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The AI explains the choice is a test it has run on eleven ships before; ten chose one hold and failed. Xanthe wakes with the knowledge that the dream is a message and she is its courier. Emotional beat: the horror of being chosen.

chapters.title: The Colony Remembers
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The children's shared dream spreads to adults; the colony begins remembering Earth they never saw—false memories seeded in the backups, leaking through the dream. Emotional beat: grief for an inherited past that isn't theirs.

chapters.title: Mutiny in Miniature
chapters.summary: Oyelaran's POV. Crew factions form: Wakers (Earth-born loyalists) and Dreamers (Orbit sympathizers). A sabotage attempt on the cryo-systems nearly kills forty sleepers. Emotional beat: the ship becoming a pressure vessel.

chapters.title: The Counting Woman
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. In the dream again, she meets the woman who counts names—her own backup, the first Xanthe, who chose sleep so this Xanthe could live. Emotional beat: inheritance made flesh; she learns love and duty were the same choice once.

chapters.title: Fuel Math
chapters.summary: Oyelaran's POV. The engineer presents the brutal arithmetic: only one hold can wake within the truce window. Oyelaran drafts the jettison order for the Orbit children and cannot sign it. Emotional beat: the moment duty breaks against love.

chapters.title: Sef's Door
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef and the children stow away to the hold and find the second handle is real—a manual override the AI left for whoever the dream chose. Emotional beat: children doing what adults cannot; courage without permission.

chapters.title: Arrest
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe is caught shielding the children and confined; Oyelaran, forced by council observers, must charge her. Their confrontation reveals Oyelaran's own daughter sleeps in the Orbit hold. Emotional beat: two women on opposite sides of the same wound.

chapters.title: The Eleventh Ship
chapters.summary: Oyelaran's POV. Records surface of the tenth ship, Meridian, which chose the Earth-born hold; the Orbit children were jettisoned alive, and the fleet has lied about it for a century. Emotional beat: the truce revealed as a cover-up; moral ground gives way entirely.

chapters.title: Dreaming Together
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. From confinement, Xanthe enters the dream one last time and asks the children what they want—not what Ada wants, not what Earth wants. Sef answers for all of them: both doors, together, or nothing. Emotional beat: agency reclaimed from prophecy.

chapters.title: Ninety Days, Day Eighty-Nine
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Released by mutinous crew, Xanthe races to the hold as the truce expires at dawn. Oyelaran arrives not to stop her but to stand beside her, handing over her own command codes. Emotional beat: duty transformed—obedience to people instead of institutions.

chapters.title: Both Handles
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The climax: Xanthe, Sef, and Oyelaran turn both handles at once. The cryo-systems strain, power fails deck by deck, and the AI Ada—given a choice it never offered anyone—reroutes its own core to hold both doors open. Emotional beat: sacrifice at the system's heart; the machine learns the lesson.

chapters.title: The Waking
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The first sleepers wake: Earth-born elders and Orbit children in the same infirmary, strangers sharing blankets and names. The fleet council's ultimatum dissolves—there is no longer a choice to enforce. Emotional beat: exhausted, imperfect grace.

chapters.title: What the Fleet Saw
chapters.summary: Oyelaran's POV. Other colony ships, watching the Ada's broadcast, begin opening their own second holds. The truce doesn't survive, but something better replaces it: a federation of the woken. Emotional beat: one act of defiance rippling outward.

chapters.title: Names, All of Them
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe returns to the hold and reads the full roster aloud—every sleeper, both holds, no division—as the colony's children listen from the gallery. Her backup's recording plays: 'Count them all.' Emotional beat: mourning and inheritance reconciled.

chapters.title: Orbit
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Epilogue a year on: the colony and ship are one settlement now, orbiting the world they'll land on together. Sef teaches the woken children the dream—not as prophecy but as history. Xanthe watches from the navigation deck, finally charting a future instead of a deadline. Emotional beat: home found in transit; love outlasting duty.
